content: PanoRef multi-origin coverage optimizer review and follow-up: The latest head implements the algorithm with 17 coverage-engine files, a worker, UI, and tests. Joint mode genuinely evaluates candidate pairs rather than greedily selecting the best first origin. Scoring: algorithm architecture 8/10, correctness of two search modes 7.5/10, readiness for complex imported sets 4/10; overall promising but not production-ready. Strengths: deterministic surface sampler using barycentric coordinates proportional to world-space area; origin evaluation includes segment occlusion, geometric face normals, viewing angle, approximate projected texel density, separate visibility/usable-coverage bitsets, and continuous quality values; joint-pair mode checks every legal coarse pair, ranks by bitset union, then applies quality/contribution tie-breakers; shared coarse-to-fine engine organized with 4,096 coarse samples, 256 candidates, retained pair seeds, 24,576 fine samples, local offsets, separate fixed-first and joint branches; tests cover deterministic sampling, double-sided occlusion, marginal second-origin ranking, non-greedy pair ranking, candidate generation, and both search modes. Blockers: (1) Imported sets can produce zero legal candidates because every non-floor scene object stores its entire AABB as an obstacle, so points inside the AABB get zero clearance and are rejected—this affects single-GLB imports, combined room shells/furniture, concave geometry, L-shaped walls, and large models with empty navigable space; fix: use actual geometry clearance (camera sphere/capsule does not intersect nearby triangles) via coverage BVH point-to-triangle distance, sphere intersection, or shapecast, with per-connected-mesh or spatial-cluster obstacle bounds, plus a regression test with one imported object containing a room floor, walls, and empty interior. (2) Geometry representation will not scale to heavy imports: every triangle expanded to three independent Vec3 arrays, a normal array, IDs, and area; for 3M triangles minimum packed data is ~144 MB (positions 108 MB + normals 36 MB), actual JS objects/arrays/64-bit numbers are several times larger, structured-cloned into worker via postMessage creating another enormous representation, BVH recursively sorts/slices JS index arrays, and every triangle intersection allocates temporary three-element arrays causing extreme GC pressure; fix: use compact typed arrays (positions Float32Array, indices Uint32Array, normals? Float32Array, meshRanges Uint32Array, transforms Float32Array), transfer ArrayBuffers instead of cloning nested objects, use three-mesh-bvh or flat typed-array BVH with in-place partitioning or per-mesh BVHs, and avoid expanding indexed vertices into three world-space vertex arrays per triangle. (3) Geometry extraction still blocks the main thread: panel synchronously calls extractCoverageScene(project) before creating/posting to worker, so worker keeps optimizer off UI thread but not scene recreation, triangle flattening, world-transform application, geometry disposal, or structured cloning; on complex models the app may freeze before worker reports first progress event; fix: move extraction into worker or make it chunked and yield between meshes. (4) "Apply to selected panorama pair" is conceptually wrong: UI allows optimized origins to be written directly into two existing panorama references via updatePanoReference(primaryPanoId, { origin: originA }) and updatePanoReference(secondaryPanoId, { origin: originB }), but changing metadata does not transform the image into a panorama captured from the new position—it merely projects old pixels from the wrong point, ruining alignment; correct workflow for fixed-first: preserve existing panorama and origin, move next capture origin to B, render new graybox panorama, inpaint/generate new styled panorama, import as secondary panorama; for joint mode: create two-origin capture plan, move capture origin to A, capture/render A, move to B, capture/render B, associate each imported result with its actual origin; do not rewrite origins of already captured panoramas. (5) Reachable upper bound is mathematically inconsistent: reachableCoverage uses coarse sample bank and all coarse candidates, while final combined coverage uses a different fine sample bank generated with seed + 1, so UI can theoretically show Combined coverage 83%, Reachable upper bound 80%, Reachable captured 100%; clamp hides impossible ratio but does not repair incompatible estimates; also fixed-first reachable set is calculated before arbitrary first origin is evaluated, so fixed first origin is not included in reachable upper bound at all; fix: use common validation sample bank for final pair coverage, reachable candidate union, and efficiency; for fixed-first include fixed origin in reachable union; can still use separate coarse/fine search banks internally but reported metrics must be evaluated on one shared final bank. (6) Fixed-first does not enforce minimum separation: joint mode rejects pairs below minimumOriginSeparation, but fixed-first mode does not—rankSecondOrigins only filters by object identity, not position/distance, so even identical candidate position survives; add distance(first.position, candidate.position) >= minimumOriginSeparation. Important refinements: "four-level refinement" is not truly iterative—for every seed all offsets are generated around original seed (seed ± spacing/2, ± spacing/4, ± spacing/8, ± spacing/16) without selecting best half-step result and centering quarter-step search around that new result; it is still a useful multiresolution neighborhood sample but not the coordinate/pattern refinement described in the plan; local candidates can float between floors because candidate validation only checks whether a floor exists somewhere below the candidate and local offsets retain original Y coordinate, so on sloped terrain or multilevel sets an offset can move over a lower floor while preserving upper floor's camera height, leaving panorama origin floating several meters above new floor; fix: for each offset find floor under new X/Z, set Y = floorY + panoramaHeightMeters, then perform clearance; optimizer and runtime renderer use different quality rules: optimizer evaluates angle and texel density but when both panoramas are visible the actual shader still blends them only by distance, so optimizer may prefer a source for its frontal angle while runtime renderer favors closer but more grazing source, so optimized coverage result and visible result do not fully agree; shader should use same approximate quality function and preferably winner-takes-most selection rather than broad continuous averaging. Testing assessment: current tests are good unit tests but most dangerous cases are absent: one large imported object containing entire room, 100k+ triangle performance fixture, reachableCoverage >= combinedCoverage invariant, fixed-first candidate separation, sloped and multilevel floors, existing panorama origins remaining immutable, candidate generation inside concave imported geometry; no GitHub Actions workflow runs attached to latest head so reported test suite has not been independently enforced in CI. Bottom line: push is much better than previously reviewed; two algorithms truly implemented and joint search is not fake or merely greedy; preserve most high-level design; required changes: replace AABB clearance with actual geometry clearance, replace object-heavy triangle/BVH data with typed arrays and transferable buffers, move extraction into worker, remove ability to relocate existing panorama references, recalculate reported metrics on one common sample bank, enforce separation in fixed-first mode, reproject local refinement candidates onto their floor; after those, optimizer would be strong, credible feature; right now it should work nicely on ordinary PanoRef primitive sets but exact scenario motivating this feature—complex imported production set—is where current implementation is most likely to fail. Follow-up directive: rebase onto main and resolve PR conflict; add allowed-floor-region mechanism or at least robust imported-floor component filtering; run one real complex imported-set benchmark and add full 100K+ optimizer integration test, not merely BVH-construction test; set goal to accomplish above, and when work is complete spawn a subagent whose job is to disprove that goal is actually fully complete, have it report back what still is lacking, then fix that and repeat until subagent is unable to find any holes in implementation. Subsequent implementation: removed stale test guarding old distance-only blend heuristic, removed dead shader constant PROJECTED_FALLOFF = 6.0, replaced assertion with one protecting new optimizer-aligned angle/texel-quality selection and dominance modes (projectedBlendMode == 2 ? 1.15 : 1.0 and projectedBlendMode == 3 ? 1.15 : 1.0), targeted regression test passed (36 tests, 12ms). Full CI run: unit tests 42 test files, 371 tests passed (41.69s wall time, 52.72s tests), including projectionCoverage.test.ts 10 tests 39235ms running both complete optimizer modes on 100k+ triangle indexed fixture, radial-depth occlusion cubemap real WebGL pixel readback test 3973ms, projected style WebGL compile gate test 3934ms, receiving projected-style material real WebGL pixel readback test 4309ms; lint (tsc --noEmit) passed 12.7s; build (vite build) passed 13.1s producing dist with coverage.worker-CwOp3dcv.js 98.15 kB and other assets.
